paras.text: (i) Speed of work

4. Good character (Good Manners)

Efficiency also depends on the good qualities of man. The labourer who is honest, sincere and noble will work with full devotion. In contrast, the labourer who is a liar, of vagrant temperament and dishonest will always shirk work; therefore his efficiency will remain low.

sections.content:
(i) Speed of work

The labourer whose speed of work is more than others, his efficiency is more, and he who works with sluggishness, his efficiency is less. It is often seen that if the same kind of work is given to two labourers, one finishes it quickly and the other late.

(ii) Standard of work

The labourer who works with refinement and excellence, his efficiency is more, and he who does work of a poor kind, his efficiency is less.

(iii) Use of raw material

The labourer who uses raw material with great care and does not let it be wasted, his efficiency is more compared with him who uses raw material carelessly.

(iv) Habits and character

The labourer who is well-mannered, honest, hard-working and responsible, his efficiency is more, but he who is ill-mannered, dishonest, lazy and irresponsible, his efficiency is less.

Factors of the productivity of labour (Factors Promoting Productivity of Labour)

The productivity of the labourer depends on the following things:

1. Physical health (Physical Health)

The labourer who is young and healthy can work more; therefore his productivity too is more. In contrast, a weak, young or old labourer cannot work well. In Pakistan, because of poverty, people’s ways of living are not clean, and food of a suitable standard is not available; therefore the efficiency of labourers is low.

2. Mental capability (Mental Capability)

The labourer who possesses good mental abilities, is sensible and understanding, will work in a better way; therefore his efficiency too will be more. In contrast, a dull and dim-witted man cannot do good work.

3. Education and training (Education and Training)

Education helps in refining man’s consciousness, and technical and mechanical training makes him able to do special work. Therefore the people who obtain technical education, their ability and productivity become more. In Pakistan (of age ten years and above) fifty-five per cent of people are educated and the rest are illiterate. In our country the standard of technical training and skill of labourers too is low. Therefore, on the whole, the productivity of Pakistani people is low.

4. Good character (Good Manners)

Efficiency also depends on the good qualities of man. The labourer who is honest, sincere and noble will work with full devotion. In contrast, the labourer who is a liar, of vagrant temperament and dishonest will always shirk work; therefore his efficiency will remain low.

5. Working conditions (Working Conditions)

The place where labourers work, if it is clean and tidy, rooms are spacious and airy, and there is arrangement of protection from the heat of the sun in summer and from cold in winter, then labourers will be able to work with ease. If conditions are the reverse, efficiency will be low. The behaviour and relations of owners too affect the efficiency of labourers.

6. Climate (Climate)

Residents living in a hot and humid climate are sluggish, and their efficiency is low. In contrast, the people of countries with a moderate climate are active and intelligent. For example, the efficiency of the labourers of Pakistan is low compared with the labourers of developed countries.

7. Spending of income (Consumption Style)

If labourers spend their income on lawful needs and comforts, an increase will occur in their efficiency. In contrast, if they spend it to fulfil bad habits like narcotics, gambling and smoking cigarettes, efficiency will remain low.

8. Opportunities of progress

If the labourer’s job is durable and there are also possibilities of progress ahead, he will work with more diligence, otherwise not.

9. Permanent job (Permanent Job)

If the labourer has complete security of his job, his employment is permanent, then he will work with more peace of mind, otherwise with reluctance.

Mobility of labour (Mobility of Labour)

On the ability and productivity of labourers this thing too has an effect, to what extent they are ready to go to different places in search of employment; as it were, whether the quality of mobility is in them or not. By the mobility of labour is meant that ability of the labourer by virtue of which he can go from one occupation to another occupation, or from one place to another place, or from the first grade of progress to the second grade. Mobility has the following kinds:

1. Geographical mobility (Geographical Mobility)

By geographical mobility is meant labourers moving from one place to another place, e.g. labourers of a factory in Faisalabad go to some factory in Karachi, or a worker of Pakistan goes to America, the Middle East and European countries for a job.

2. Occupational mobility (Occupational Mobility)

If some labourer leaves an occupation of one kind and adopts some other occupation, this will be occupational mobility, e.g. some barber starts the work of a tailor, or a clerk becomes a school teacher.

3. Parallel or horizontal mobility (Horizontal Mobility)

By it is meant that some person leaves one factory or office and becomes employed at the same post in another office or factory, e.g. an accountant leaves a job of WAPDA and goes to some bank.

5. Working conditions (Working Conditions)

The place where labourers work, if it is clean and tidy, rooms are spacious and airy, and there is arrangement of protection from the heat of the sun in summer and from cold in winter, then labourers will be able to work with ease. If conditions are the reverse, efficiency will be low. The behaviour and relations of owners too affect the efficiency of labourers.

6. Climate (Climate)

Residents living in a hot and humid climate are sluggish, and their efficiency is low. In contrast, the people of countries with a moderate climate are active and intelligent. For example, the efficiency of the labourers of Pakistan is low compared with the labourers of developed countries.

7. Spending of income (Consumption Style)

If labourers spend their income on lawful needs and comforts, an increase will occur in their efficiency. In contrast, if they spend it to fulfil bad habits like narcotics, gambling and smoking cigarettes, efficiency will remain low.

8. Opportunities of progress

If the labourer’s job is durable and there are also possibilities of progress ahead, he will work with more diligence, otherwise not.

9. Permanent job (Permanent Job)

If the labourer has complete security of his job, his employment is permanent, then he will work with more peace of mind, otherwise with reluctance.

Mobility of labour (Mobility of Labour)

On the ability and productivity of labourers this thing too has an effect, to what extent they are ready to go to different places in search of employment; as it were, whether the quality of mobility is in them or not. By the mobility of labour is meant that ability of the labourer by virtue of which he can go from one occupation to another occupation, or from one place to another place, or from the first grade of progress to the second grade. Mobility has the following kinds:

1. Geographical mobility (Geographical Mobility)

By geographical mobility is meant labourers moving from one place to another place, e.g. labourers of a factory in Faisalabad go to some factory in Karachi, or a worker of Pakistan goes to America, the Middle East and European countries for a job.

2. Occupational mobility (Occupational Mobility)

If some labourer leaves an occupation of one kind and adopts some other occupation, this will be occupational mobility, e.g. some barber starts the work of a tailor, or a clerk becomes a school teacher.

3. Parallel or horizontal mobility (Horizontal Mobility)

By it is meant that some person leaves one factory or office and becomes employed at the same post in another office or factory, e.g. an accountant leaves a job of WAPDA and goes to some bank.
